name: International Lunar Research Station (ILRS)
short_status: In development: 13 national members as of July 2026; Chang'e-7 precursor launch postponed on 23 Aug 2026 with no new date announced (as of 2 Nov 2026); basic station targeted 2035 at the lunar south pole.
tagline: CNSA and Roscosmos · Multinational · Programme · 2021 · Commercial and multipolar In development
stats: member countries as of July 2026, China and Russia included
target year for the basic station at the lunar south pole
researchers China aims to recruit, alongside 50 countries and 500 institutions
discussed delivery window for the Russian lunar nuclear reactor

facts.label: Roadmap and Guide for Partnership unveiled
Coordinating body
facts.value: ILRSCO, announced 25 April 2023; HQ planned in Deep Space Science City, Hefei

facts.label: National members (as of July 17, 2026)
facts.value: 13: China, Russia, Venezuela, South Africa, Azerbaijan, Pakistan, Belarus, Egypt, Thailand, Nicaragua, Serbia, Kazakhstan, Senegal

facts.label: CNSA aggregate count (April 24, 2025)
facts.value: 17 countries and international organizations; 50+ research institutions

facts.label: Extended-phase target (two official framings)
facts.value: Expanded station by 2045 (April 2025); Moon-wide network by 2050 (September 2024)

facts.label: Chang'e-7 precursor
facts.value: Launch postponed: on 23 Aug 2026 the China Manned Space Engineering Office said Chang'e-7 does not meet launch conditions and cannot fly in this year's scheduled window; no new date announced (as of 2 Nov 2026); south pole water-ice hunt with orbiter, lander, rover, hopper

facts.label: Chang'e-8 precursor
facts.value: Targeted around 2029 per CNSA (April 2025); ISRU tests including regolith brick-making; 30 kg Pakistani SUPARCO rover. SpaceNews reported on 10 Sep 2026 that China appears to be reconfiguring its robotic Moon program, Chang'e 8 included; no Chinese official source has announced a change (as of 2 Nov 2026)

facts.label: Lunar nuclear power plant
facts.value: China-Russia MOU May 2025; reactor delivery discussed 2033-2035; Roscosmos-Lavochkin contract December 2025, plant stated for 2036

facts.label: Russian segment concept approved
facts.value: Russian Academy of Sciences approval announced 1 April 2026

facts.label: Counterpart bloc
facts.value: Artemis Accords: 78 signatories as of 2 November 2026 (Vietnam 78th, 28 October 2026)

facts.label: Members of both blocs
facts.value: Thailand, Senegal (24 July 2025) and Serbia (16 July 2026)

timeline: China and Russia sign the ILRS memorandum of understanding
Joint roadmap and Guide for Partnership presented at GLEX 2021, St. Petersburg
ILRSCO coordinating organization announced at Hefei deep-space conference; APSCO signs joint statement
Venezuela becomes the first national member beyond the founders; five more countries join through Dec 2023
Wu Weiren unveils the 50 countries / 500 institutions / 5,000 researchers goal at China Space Day
Jun 2024
Putin signs the law ratifying the Russia-China ILRS cooperation agreement
Senegal joins as the 13th national member (still the newest as of Jul 2026)
CNSA: 17 countries and international organizations, 50+ institutions signed on
May 2025
CNSA and Roscosmos sign memorandum on a lunar nuclear power station during Xi's Moscow visit
ILRS member Senegal signs the Artemis Accords (56th signatory), second country in both blocs
Dec 2025
Roscosmos signs state contract with NPO Lavochkin for the lunar power plant, stated for completion by 2036
Russian Academy of Sciences approves the concept for Russia's ILRS segment, per Roscosmos chief Bakanov
May 2026
Omani firm Oman Lens signs ILRS partnership with DSEL; Serbia signs Artemis Accords 16 Jul 2026 while remaining an ILRS member
Chang'e-7 launch postponed: does not meet launch conditions, cannot fly in this year's scheduled window (CMSE); no new date announced as of 2 Nov 2026
Around 2029
Targeted: Chang'e-8 in-situ resource utilization demo (CNSA target since Apr 2025; SpaceNews reported a reconfiguration on 10 Sep 2026 that no Chinese official source had announced as of 2 Nov 2026)
Planned: five ILRS construction missions; basic station complete by 2035
Planned: expanded station by 2045 per Apr 2025 statements; Moon-wide network by 2050 per Sep 2024 statements
